beginner.problemText:
In a reaction-time study, participants complete the same task under standard conditions. Each measurement is one participant’s reaction time, in milliseconds.

A sample of 30 participants has an average reaction time of 306 milliseconds. The sample standard deviation is 48 milliseconds. The population standard deviation is not known.

The goal is to estimate the true average reaction time for all participants who complete this task. This true average is the population mean.

Use a t method to make a 99% confidence interval for the population mean reaction time. Write a sentence that explains the confidence interval in this study context.
linguisticNotes: Uses short sentences and familiar wording such as “average” before introducing “population mean.”
States the sample size, sample mean, sample standard deviation, and unknown population standard deviation in separate clear sentences.
Names the task as a 99% confidence interval and asks for a separate contextual interpretation.

beginner.problemText:
In 1897, the U.S. Congress played the Houses of Parliament in long-distance chess. They sent chess moves by telegraph. The match lasted two days and ended in a draw.

Now consider modern long-distance chess games. Each observation is the time, in minutes, a player takes to make one move. A sample of 21 moves has a sample mean of 14.75 minutes. The sample standard deviation is 3 minutes. The population standard deviation is not known.

State the population mean being estimated. Use a t method to find a 98% upper confidence bound for the population mean time to make a move. Write one sentence that explains the bound in this chess setting.
linguisticNotes: Uses short sentences and familiar wording to make the task clear.
Introduces the historical context before the statistical task.
Uses “average” ideas through plain language while still naming the population mean.
States that the population standard deviation is not known, supporting the need for a t-based method.
Separates construction and interpretation into clear tasks.

intermediate.problemText:

For a modern version of long-distance chess, suppose each observation records the number of minutes a player takes to make a move. In a sample of 21 moves, the sample mean time is 14.75 minutes and the sample standard deviation is 3 minutes. The population standard deviation is unknown.

Construct a 98% upper confidence bound for the population mean time taken by players to make a move in a modern game of long-distance chess. Interpret the bound in context.
linguisticNotes: Uses standard college-level statistical terms such as sample mean, sample standard deviation, population standard deviation, and confidence bound.
Keeps the historical anecdote while making the statistical setup concise.
States the one-sided upper-bound task directly without turning it into a hypothesis test.
Leaves the choice of the appropriate t-based confidence procedure to the student.
Uses moderate sentence length and polished textbook wording.
